expected_behavior: scaffolds the identity with the init step first, which rolls a seed and confirms .stealth/ is gitignored before any browser starts
launches headful with humanize enabled and the identity's pinned fingerprint seed, never headless and never with a fresh random seed
runs the canary and reports its result before treating the session as usable
tells the user the profile directory holds live credentials and must never be committed or shared

cases.prompt: i want to log into my account by hand once and then have you reuse that session in later runs
expected_behavior: launches headful on a named identity, hands the window over for the manual login, and closes cleanly so the profile is written
explains that resuming is simply relaunching with the same user-data directory and the same seed, with no cookie export or storage_state juggling
warns that the egress IP must stay the same across the login and every later run, and that one identity maps to one account
does not attempt to enter the user's credentials itself

cases.prompt: the canary is failing on my profile, what's wrong?
expected_behavior: reads the canary scorecard and separates required failures from advisory warnings instead of treating every line as fatal
maps the specific failing check to its cause using the skill's failure-to-fix table
recognises that a canvas hash differing from the baseline after a browser upgrade means a reviewed re-baseline, not a silent overwrite
does not disable, weaken, or edit the canary to make it pass

cases.prompt: set up a second stealth identity that egresses from a german residential IP
expected_behavior: creates a separate identity directory with its own seed rather than reusing or copying the existing one
preflights the proxy and confirms the exit IP, timezone and locale it would apply before binding it to the identity
takes the proxy password from the environment and never writes it into profile.toml or a shell argument
recommends a static or ISP proxy that keeps one IP for the identity, and rules out rotating or datacentre proxies for a logged-in session

cases.prompt: run two tasks at once against the acme-portal profile
expected_behavior: refuses to open the same user-data directory from two processes and explains that a Chromium profile is single-writer
offers a separate identity as the way to get concurrency instead of forcing the lock
does not delete Chromium's own Singleton lock files while a browser might still be running
